channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [8] Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ at sub-unit-cell resolution
item.description:
Last authors: Wentao Zhang, Peng Gao

Authors: Xiaowen Zhang, Jiade Li, Xiaoyue Gao, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-resolution spectroscopy of phonons and superconducting gap in a classic cuprate superconductor.

Tags: #cuprates #superconductivity #spectroscopy

Abstract: The role of phonons in cuprate superconductivity remains debated, partly because their layered structures host complex lattice dynamics. Here, sub-unit-cell spectroscopy resolves layer-localized phonons in Bi-2212 and reveals a spatial correlation between superstructure-driven phonon frequency modulations and superconducting gap variations.

item.title: [7] Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
item.description:
Last authors: Hyeongseop Kim, H.-S. Sim

Authors: Kyungtae Kim, June-Young M. Lee, Hyeongseop Kim, H.-S. Sim

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Proposal for Majorana manipulation in topological insulator junctions, highly relevant to topological superconductivity interests.

Tags: #Majorana #topologicalinsulator #superconductivity

Abstract: Manipulating Majorana bound states is a key requirement for topological quantum computation. Here, the authors propose a topological insulator Josephson trijunction in a magnetic field that enables the generation, transport, and fusion of Majorana bound states through static control of superconducting phases.
